clue.text: More attractive means of holding an international frolic

indicators.note: holding means the first word for more attractive keeps the other pieces held within it

parts.note: more attractive means cuter
a cap is awarded for each appearance in a national team, so an international is a cap

explanation.surface: Someone weighs up a more attractive way of getting hold of a foreign romp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' is the container signal; in sport a player who represents their country is said to win a cap, so the players themselves are internationals.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut a caper is an idiom for leaping about playfully, which is what a frolic is.

clue.text: Yields obtained from plants, it is said

indicators.note: it is said tells us the word for things obtained from plants is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: seeds are what are obtained from plants for sowing

explanation.surface: A remark about crop harvests taken from growing plants.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to surrender or give up, so cedes is a synonym for yields as a verb.

clue.text: Visitor getting to old city first

parts.note: taken as written
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia, the crossword's favourite old city
first is written 1st, and the digit 1 stands for the letter I, giving IST

explanation.surface: A traveller makes for an ancient city before anywhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: A sightseer is a visitor to a place, the everyday synonym here.

clue.text: Volumes of instruction man copied out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the following words are put into disorder and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instruction manuals transcribed by a scribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copied out' reads as one phrase, but 'out' alone is the anagram signal on MAN plus COPIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Compendia are comprehensive reference works that sum up a subject, so they are books of teaching.

clue.text: Breakthrough achieved by means of fine speech

parts.note: per is Latin for through or by means of, as in per post
F stands for fine, as on pencil grades
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A breakthrough is reached through a splendid address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breakthrough' suggests a discovery, but here it is literal: a hole broken through something.
explanation.definitionFit: A perforation is a hole pierced right through a material, literally a break through it.

clue.text: The odd drink

definitions.meaning: old-fashioned British slang for strange or peculiar
a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both strange, in dated British slang, and a spirit made from sugar cane.

clue.text: Cast enables fellow to get fish

parts.note: the ling is an edible sea fish related to the cod

explanation.surface: A cast of the line lets a man land a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To fling is to throw hard, which is a synonym for cast.

clue.text: They depend on the host for entertainment — generally inside to begin with

parts.note: fun is amusement or entertainment

indicators.note: to begin with tells us to take only the opening letter of each of the words generally and inside

explanation.surface: Guests count on their host to provide amusement, usually indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The host is not a party-giver but the organism a parasite lives on.
explanation.definitionFit: Many fungi are parasites that live off a host organism such as a tree.

clue.text: Single girl in charge holding ancient book collection — that's senseless

indicators.note: holding means the first three pieces keep the old scriptures within them

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one, a single
Di is a short girl's name, for Diana
OT is the Old Testament, an ancient collection of books

explanation.surface: An unmarried woman running an old library seems to be making no sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something idiotic is foolish and lacks sense, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Development of energy embracing everybody as a rule

indicators.note: embracing means the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside them
development of means the letters of energy are worked into a new form

parts.note: all means everybody

explanation.surface: Building up energy that takes in the whole population is the norm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Development of' rearranges the six letters of energy to GENERY, and 'embracing' puts the word for everybody inside, after the N and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Generally means usually or in most cases, an exact synonym of the phrase as a rule.

clue.text: Common thief who might beat the snares ?

definitions.meaning: old slang for a thief, especially a burglar

explanation.definitionFit: The word is old slang for a thief and also the musician who plays the drums, snare drums included.

clue.text: An indication of military distinction

parts.note: a soldier honoured for bravery may be named in despatches, an official notice of merit

explanation.definitionFit: Being mentioned in despatches is a British military honour for gallantry noted in an officer's report.

clue.text: Excel in Polish, say?

definitions.meaning: to buff something until it gleams

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to stand out brilliantly and also to buff shoes until they gleam.

clue.text: He equips one for discharge in a healthier state

parts.note: a patient discharged from hospital is out
fitter means in better health

explanation.surface: A patient leaves hospital feeling better.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests hospital discharge; 'for' links the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter sells clothing and equipment, supplying someone with gear.

clue.text: He may remove branches in our greenest organisation

indicators.note: organisation means the letters of the preceding words are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: An environmental group says it may cut down branches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'branches' suggests local offices of the green organisation, but they are a tree's limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: An arborist who looks after trees prunes or lops their limbs.

clue.text: Winger or striker

definitions.meaning: a flying mammal, something with wings
a club for hitting the ball in cricket or baseball

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a flying mammal with wings and a club used to hit a ball.

clue.text: Strand dance with bouncer

parts.note: a strand is a shore or beach
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A seaside party with a doorman on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncer' suggests a nightclub doorman, but it is just something that bounces.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable ball bounces, so it is playfully called a bouncer.

clue.text: Utterly opposed to broadcasting dramatic lie

indicators.note: broadcasting means scattering widely, so the letters of the next words are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is firmly against a station airing a sensational falsehood.
explanation.definitionFit: Diametrical describes things at opposite ends of a diameter, hence completely contrary.

clue.text: Complaint reinforcing reprimand in course of meal

indicators.note: reinforcing means propping up from below, so in this down entry the complaint comes beneath the reprimand

parts.note: to roast someone is to criticise them severely
beef is slang for a grievance

explanation.surface: A diner grumbles and tells off the waiter during dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'reinforcing' puts BEEF under ROAST, holding it up.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint of oven-cooked beef is a main dish, one part of a dinner.

clue.text: Navigating is a credit among drivers in waterway

indicators.note: among means the rearranged letters go in between the motoring letters

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, the British motoring organisation for drivers

indicators.note: navigating means steering a course around, so the letters of the next words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Steering a course is considered to a motorist's honour on a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Navigating' rearranges IS A CREDIT; 'among' sets those letters between the letters for the British motoring organisation used by drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adriatic is an arm of the Mediterranean between Italy and the Balkans, a body of water.

clue.text: Unusual morsel found in dish

parts.note: rare means unusual
a bit is a small piece or morsel

explanation.surface: An odd scrap turns up on a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is a British dish of melted cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is a savoury food of cheese sauce on toast, a dish.

clue.text: Sally, oddly, is underhanded

indicators.note: oddly tells us to keep the letters in odd positions of the name, the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Sally is behaving strangely and deceitfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Sly means cunning and secretive, a synonym for underhanded.

clue.text: Term that's left to describe King Charles, perhaps

parts.note: a span is a period of time, a term
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A word remaining to sum up a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: King Charles is not the monarch but the King Charles spaniel, a toy dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The King Charles is a breed of small dog of the spaniel type, so it is an example.

clue.text: Uncompromising type gets difficult introduction to vessel

parts.note: a hard start is a difficult introduction; to is a link
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A tough customer has a rough start boarding a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardliner is a person who sticks rigidly to policy, refusing to give ground.

clue.text: Soil deficiency seen around the middle of Kew?

indicators.note: around means the word for deficiency goes round the central letter

parts.note: a loss is a shortfall or deficiency

indicators.note: the middle of means only the central letter of the name Kew is used

explanation.surface: A gardener notices poor earth in the centre of Kew.
explanation.walkthrough: Kew is the Royal Botanic Gardens in London, which suits the soil surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Loess is a fine windblown silt that forms fertile earth, a kind of soil.

clue.text: Large number in vehicle, so walk

indicators.note: in means the large number goes inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a trap is a light horse-drawn carriage
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a large number

explanation.surface: A crowd packs into a bus, so someone goes on foot instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk heavily or a long way, a synonym of walk.

clue.text: Make an insistent demand for newspapers

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to urge someone strongly and also the newspapers collectively.

clue.text: A doctor — one with speciality concerned with the environment

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
the Roman numeral I is one
ENT, ear nose and throat, is a medical speciality

explanation.surface: A medic with a specialism takes an interest in green issues.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambient describes the surrounding conditions, relating to one's surroundings.

clue.text: Leaderless pack in drag

indicators.note: leaderless means the word for pack loses its first letter

parts.note: to stow is to pack away

explanation.surface: A pack without its chief is pulled about.
explanation.definitionFit: To tow is to pull along behind, a synonym of drag.

clue.text: One seeking privacy to relax amid ease, we hear

indicators.note: amid means the relaxing word sits in the middle of the spoken letters
we hear means the word ease is sounded, giving its sound-alike, two letter Es

parts.note: ease sounds like Es, the plural of the letter E
to remit is to relax or slacken, as in remitting a penalty

explanation.surface: A recluse wants to unwind in comfort, so it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns ease into its sound-alike, E's, two letter Es, which go round REMIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a hermit, a religious recluse who withdraws from the world.

clue.text: Bloomer made by many going to America

parts.note: a lot means many
US is the United States, America

explanation.surface: A blunder is made by many heading for the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder, but it is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily that flowers, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: Fruit drops required for air trips

parts.note: wind is moving air
falls are trips or tumbles

explanation.surface: Fruit needs a breeze and some stumbles to come down.
explanation.definitionFit: Windfalls are apples or other fruit blown off a tree by the wind.
